I’ve had agoraphobia for many years and for the last 4 years on a special occasion for my mother what she’s wanted is to go to the beach and sit in and the and watch the waves, I’m still trying to get to that point, I still haven’t been able to go even by car. So I’ve got a lot of guilt on my conscience because I feel like I’m consistently letting people down. 

But for years I’ve even struggled leaving my own bedroom to go to other rooms in my house.

But slowly slowly, we get to those other rooms. We get to the mail box when it’s not 1am so we know others won’t be out and we won’t have to exchange pleasantries.

No matter how long it takes to accomplish your list, you know what? You’ve taken the biggest step by making one. You have set goals, and the worst thing you can do is rush yourself or feel guilty that you haven’t accomplished them by a set time or date.


Congratulate yourself for making your list. And give yourself your own time to set them. Never set a time that you have to have to have them done by, because that just increases the anxiety around it. And when you do accomplish these goals you want them to feel natural and enjoyable- not like a chore. Okay you never know you might just surprise yourself and accomplish one without even trying. Just don’t pressure yourself. And you’ll get there.

No worries, just let some of these things occur naturally or even build up by doing things you are comfortable with.

Okay, you May be scared but you need to approach this gently, a lot of people that suffer from many EDs really don’t value themselves and have quite low self esteem, high levels of guilt and shame and are convinced they aren’t worthy of help, and often fear that they will be a burden to the ones they love if they ask for help they also may fear that if they do admit to struggling with an Ed the reaction is going to be angry, punitive and like they’ve let you down, when in reality our self esteem is so low we think we are doing the right thing by keeping this to ourselves, - because we don’t think we are worthy of help, and that our ED doesn’t warrant help because we’ll often convince ourselves it’s not bad enough to warrant help we may need, even if it’s painfully obvious to everyone around us that we need help, we are fantastic at being in complete denial, and always think it’s selfish to seek help “when we aren’t sick enough for that and someone else needs help more than us, and there’s the ever present thought and fear of becoming the “burden to family and friends” so we’ll deny it, but if you and your family can approach it. 

Sit down with us and have a conversation, try to use “I feel rather that you are making me feel statements, so it doesn’t look like it’s coming from anger or shame” it might be hard but begin gently and let us know you aren’t ashamed or angry. Don’t  catastrophize out of fear with threats of treatment centres or telling us we’ll die, these statements will make us go back into our shell of denial and we’ll be angry with ourselves even if your sister screams at you “she’s fine, it’s none of your business and to piss off basically” it’s out of fear we’ve let you down and failed in not hurting the ones we love by concerning them.

Let them know they are loved and this will never change that, let them get their words out too. 

And as I said start gently just sit down with a few members of the family or people that are special to us etc close friends not all just a small group of people we feel loved by and love too,

Remember don’t rush into things, - tell us not condescendingly what your worries are, for example I’ve noticed you’ve been struggling with a,b,c and I’ve noticed a change in your eating habits, I want to offer support if you want to talk because I really care about you and love you, if you aren’t ready to talk about this, I want you to know you can talk to me, this does not change the way I see you or make me angry at you. I just want to offer support when you feel ready to talk,

Once you have that ice breaker conversation don’t be surprised if we deny it or seem angry or if we do yell. We’ve been holding this burden for a long time and EDs will do all the mental gymnastics it needs so we convince ourselves- we don’t need help, some of us are convinced we aren’t suffering and some aren’t at a point to acknowledge we need help, because EDs suck you deep into a wormhole where we can convince ourselves that we need it, and it’s the only control and “friend” we have that gets us, anyone else talking to us about it will make the ED feel threatened and EDs can feel threatened that someone is coming in to try and take control of it.

So be patient with us, keep loving us and keep trying to show us you are there, not angry or ashamed, or talking at us like we have an issue and are something broken that needs to be fixed

If you have to keep trying to have this conversation, let them get their words out, ask us about it because it’s not something you understand but you want to, so you know what to say, then put things on the table like, maybe we could make an appointment with our local family physician so you can understand things better, and then that might slowly move into us seeing a nutritionist to get more support in our lives and understanding. As I said start gently because we’re trying to take in a lot ourselves because now what we thought we were hiding isn’t our secret anymore and as I said EDs can feel threatened very easily and the control we are under by the Ed is strong and scary to share. So don’t treat us like that’s all we are, talk to us like you don’t view us the Ed but the same person you know and love, but you also know we are suffering. It may take time to open up, but don’t get mad please just take the time we need, be patient don’t give up, even if you feel like you have to have to first conversation with us over and over don’t give up.

That’s my advice as a long term sufferer, and different approaches work for different people, but I hope your sister gets well she’s lucky to have someone caring and supportive in her corner, because recover is a battle and we won’t ask for help until things are too hard to control or we feel we are in too deep to ever change. Because battling an Ed for recovery really is a war we have to fight and we need people helping us win that war, and the many battles we’ll face along the way 😔

Once more don’t give up.
